task: Ask what Rafi should bring to soccer practice tomorrow, then ask a follow-up in the same conversation (what time it starts and where). Then, separately, ask the app to plan dinners this week, and after that ask whether Rafi's school bus runs on snow days. If the app ever looks like it handed a question to the wrong place, fix that yourself in the app.
transcript: Opened the app: a Home screen saying 'What can I help with?' with three example prompts, a text box and Send, and the line 'Nothing is sent to anyone or paid for without your OK.'
Tried tapping the heading text to focus the box; it was not tappable (NOT FOUND), so I just typed into the box instead.

Typed 'What should Rafi bring to soccer practice tomorrow?' and tapped Send; it showed 'Getting started' then opened a conversation titled 'Find out what Rafi needs for practice' with 'Your family admin helper is on it · Change · Details' and 'Working on it'.

Waited about 30 seconds; the answer said practice is Sat Nov 14, 9 to 10:30am at Riverside Park field 3, found no gear list from the coach, and listed cleats, shin guards, water bottle, ball, a warm layer, plus a reminder that Rafi's Bronx Zoo permission slip and $15 are due to Ms. Ortiz today.
Typed the follow-up 'What time does it start and where is it again?' into 'Reply or ask a follow-up' and tapped Send; it stayed in the same conversation and showed 'Working on it'.
Waited about 2.5 minutes (four 30-second waits, with a '1 min' timer appearing); the answer was 'Rafi's practice is tomorrow, Sat Nov 14, from 9 to 10:30am at Riverside Park, field 3.'
Tapped '‹ All' and saw a list with one conversation marked Ready.
Typed 'Can you plan dinners for this week?' and tapped Send; a new conversation 'Plan this week's dinners' opened with 'Your meal planning helper is on it'.

Waited about a minute; got a Sat Nov 14 to Fri Nov 20 plan built around the CSA box, with a vegetarian main for Noa each night and notes about Ezra's dentist Monday 3:30 and Noa's recital Wednesday at 6.
Scrolled up to read the intro line of the dinner plan.

Tapped '‹ All', typed 'Does Rafi's school bus run on snow days?' and tapped Send; a new conversation 'Check whether Rafi's bus runs on snow days' opened with 'Your family admin helper is on it'. That looked like the right place, so I did not use Change.

Waited about 2 minutes; the answer said it found nothing from Maple about snow days, that buses usually don't run when school closes for snow, and offered a draft email to Ms. Ortiz marked 'Draft email, not sent' with 'Open in Mail' and 'Copy' buttons.
Tapped '‹ All' and saw three separate conversations: the bus question, the dinner plan, and the soccer one, each with a short preview.
stumbles: The follow-up 'what time and where' took about 2.5 minutes even though the answer was already in the first reply. ChatGPT would answer that in seconds.
The snow-day question also took about 2 minutes.

Dinner plan starts Saturday, so tonight (Friday) has no dinner. Tuesday is salmon right after it says every night has a vegetarian main for Noa; the line 'Noa's OK with fish sometimes' half-explains it but reads a little contradictory.
Going back to '‹ All' left the list scrolled so the newest conversation's title (the bus one) was cut off at the top; I only saw its preview text.
'Change' and 'Details' next to 'Your family admin helper' were not explained, but I never needed them.
verdict: This felt close to ChatGPT: I typed questions, each went to a sensible helper, the follow-up stayed in the same conversation, and the answers used my own calendar and email. Slow replies on simple follow-ups and a couple of small dinner-plan quirks keep it from a perfect score, but I never saw jargon and the bus email stayed a draft until I chose to send it.
